Name: Love Canal
Description: The warning Niagara could not ignore. Hooker Chemical buried roughly 21,000 tons of chemical waste here between 1942 and 1952.

Name: Electromet · Union Carbide
Location: South of Pine Avenue, east of Packard Road, Niagara Falls, NY
Description: Manhattan Project uranium metal production: uranium tetrafluoride was reduced to uranium metal, generating radioactive slag and residues.

Name: Hooker Chemical · Buffalo Avenue
Location: Buffalo Avenue at 47th Street, Niagara Falls, NY
Description: Chemical industry, uranium-recovery context, the 1975 chlorine tank-car explosion, and asbestos-worker history.

Name: Goodyear Chemical
Description: Active industrial context within the Buffalo Avenue manufacturing corridor.

Name: Carborundum · Buffalo Avenue
Location: 23 Acheson Drive / Buffalo Avenue, Niagara Falls, NY
Description: Final Niagara-area industrial leg in the project’s uranium route before the waste route to LOOW/NFSS.

Name: Highland Avenue
Description: Vanadium, Airco, SKW and Globe: heavy metallurgy, slag, landfill history and off-site fill reuse.

Name: Union Carbide landfill · Newco / CECOS
Location: 5600 Niagara Falls Boulevard, Niagara Falls, NY
Description: A key node in the regional waste network where Union Carbide material was buried, hauled, sold and reused.

Name: LOOW · Niagara Falls Storage Site
Description: Former Lake Ontario Ordnance Works and the federal Niagara Falls Storage Site; Manhattan Project and Atomic Energy Commission waste storage and consolidation.

Name: Model City · the patchwork beyond NFSS
Location: Pletcher Road / Balmer Road / Model City Road, Model City, NY
Description: CWM and Modern Disposal on separate former-LOOW tracts; later radiological findings show that the history extends beyond the federal boundary.

Name: Bell Aircraft · Bell Aerospace
Location: Former Bell Wheatfield plant · Niagara Falls Boulevard / Walmore Road
Description: X-1 and Mach 1, X-2, RASCAL nuclear missile work, rocket propulsion, vertical-flight research, space systems and the environmental afterlife of rocket testing.
